fixes.explanation: Water, baker. The verse says it plainly: “…there was no water for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:1) A whole nation camped at Rephidim, and the one thing missing was a drink. That's a campsite review with one star and one sentence.
The LORD. Moses asks, “Why do you test the LORD?” (Exodus 17:2) The people had been contending with Moses, and his question brings the LORD into it. I bet he said it with one eyebrow up, too.
The text doesn't send Moses looking for Aaron here. It says Moses cried out to the LORD. (Exodus 17:4) He asks, “What should I do with these people?” That's a question for God.

No tent-hiding in this scene. The verse says Moses cried out to the LORD. (Exodus 17:4) He says, “A little more and they will stone me!” I'll admit, if I were him I'd be looking for the nearest door. Moses cries out to the LORD instead.

That's the one. The LORD says, “Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.” (Exodus 17:5) It's the same staff Moses struck the Nile with. Then the LORD says He will stand by the rock at Horeb. (Exodus 17:6)

Strikes. The LORD says, “And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:6) He also says He will stand there before Moses by the rock. So the water comes out of it with the LORD standing right there.

It's the other way around, friend. The text says Moses did this “…in the sight of the elders of Israel.” (Exodus 17:6) The LORD had told him to take some of the elders along. (Exodus 17:5) That's a lot of eyes on one rock.

Quarreled. The verse says Moses named the place that “…because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD…” (Exodus 17:7) The text gives two reasons, and quarreling is the first. Some places get named for the view. This one got named for what the people did.

Resting isn't one of the reasons in this verse, baker. Moses named the place because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD. (Exodus 17:7) The name points back to the quarreling and the testing.

Joshua. Moses tells him, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites.” (Exodus 17:9) The next verse says Joshua did as Moses had instructed him. (Exodus 17:10) Moses gives the order, and Joshua carries it out.

Gideon is from much later, friend. His story is in the book of Judges. (Judges 6:11) In this scene, Moses gives the order to Joshua: “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites.” (Exodus 17:9) Different era for Gideon, but a good name to know.

Hilltop. Moses says, “Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.” (Exodus 17:9) Joshua is the one told to go out and fight, and Moses takes the hilltop. That hilltop ends up mattering a lot.

Moses isn't shouting orders down the hill in this verse. It says, “As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed…” (Exodus 17:11) The verse puts the weight on his hands, not on calling out to Joshua.
Sun. Their help kept his hands steady “…until the sun went down.” (Exodus 17:12) That's the end point the verse gives. His hands had grown heavy, so I'm glad he had company, baker.

Reminder. The LORD says, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua…” (Exodus 17:14) So the command is to write it down and say it out loud. Good habit, baker. I keep my recipes written down too.

The LORD Is My Banner. Moses built an altar and named it that. (Exodus 17:15) Then he said, “…The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.” (Exodus 17:16) The name points straight to the LORD.

That's a real name from the Bible, baker, but it's another story. Abraham named a place The LORD Will Provide. (Genesis 22:14) Here, Moses names his altar The LORD Is My Banner. (Exodus 17:15) Different man, different place.
